## The ask

PR 2022 added `crew finish <lane>`: it finishes a stopped lean lane and stops committed and rebased, with a
`finish-ready` row and nothing pushed. Add the operator's decision on a ready lane, as ADR-051 section 3 describes:

- `crew finish <lane> --accept [--notes <file>]` publishes the PR, with the operator's notes under their own heading
  in the body.
- `crew finish <lane> --return <file>` runs one more finish pass with the file's guidance as the builder's triage
  input.
- `crew finish <lane> --abandon` ends it; nothing is published.

Each decision is a `finish-decision` journal row with the choice and the notes' sha256 digest (null when no notes).
A green finish run also writes one fused finish report, so the deciding session reads it instead of the journal.

Invariants:
- A decision verb acts only on a lane whose last run ended `finish-ready` and that has no decision since.
- `--accept` publishes exactly the subject and body the finish run measured, plus the notes; merging stays the
  operator's.
- After `--accept`, `crew closeout <lane>` accepts the lane (it reads the journal's last `pr` row).
- A `--return` pass counts against the finish run's three-round review cap; it never grants new rounds.
- `crew finish <lane>` with no flag behaves exactly as today.

## Context

- `docs/adr/adr-051-finish-shape.md` section 3: the report, the three verbs, the decision row.
- `crew/loop.mjs`: the PR body is built at line 357 from `measurements`; a finish run emits `finish-ready` at 377
  with only `head`. The decision needs the run's subject and body, and the report needs the stop it finished, each
  review verdict with its findings, and the gate, proof and suite measurements.
- `crew/finish.mjs`: `finishLane` builds the finish spec and spawns the run; its refusals and the per-stop claim are
  above that; `main` takes only the lane today.
- `crew/checks.mjs` `openPullRequest` (line 578) is the publish seam the standard loop uses; `crew/record-pr.mjs`
  shows the `pr` row shape `crew closeout` reads.
- `bin/crew.mjs` usage lines and `bin/crew.test.mjs` for the verb.

## Acceptance

- (FD1) a green finish run writes a finish report in the lane task dir that names the stop reason it finished.
- (FD2) the finish report lists each review verdict of the run with its findings.
- (FD3) `crew finish <lane> --accept` opens the PR with the finish run's subject as its title.
- (FD4) `--accept --notes <file>` puts the file's text in the PR body under its own heading.
- (FD5) `--accept` appends a `pr` row that `crew closeout` reads as the lane's PR.
- (FD6) `--abandon` appends a `finish-decision` row with choice `abandon` and opens no PR.
- (FD7) `--return <file>` starts a finish run whose builder's first feedback carries the file's text.
- (FD8) a decision verb on a lane whose last run did not end `finish-ready` is refused as `finish-not-ready`.
- (FD9) a second decision on the same ready lane is refused as `finish-decided`.
